verdicts.claim: evidence[0] — stinkCloudRenderer.ts:132: `ensureAtlas()` sits at :138, BELOW the `world.stinkClouds.size === 0` early return at :132-137. 'THE ROOT CAUSE.'
verdicts.note: The QUOTE is verbatim and the line numbers are exact — I read src/render/stinkCloudRenderer.ts:130-138: `sync(world: World): void { this.haze.clear(); if (world.stinkClouds.size === 0) { ... this.reapAllSprites(); return; } this.ensureAtlas();`. The ordering claim is CONFIRMED. Calling it THE ROOT CAUSE is not. Two facts kill it as a root cause: (a) `stinkCloudRenderer.sync(world)` runs on EVERY ticker frame from boot — it sits at main.ts:4052, OUTSIDE the `if (world.gameState === 'PLAYING') {` block that opens at main.ts:3951 and closes at :3956 — and a bag cannot be clicked until it is in `world.stinkClouds` (controls.ts:766 `for (const bag of this.world.stinkClouds.values())`), so `ensureAtlas()` necessarily fires on the same frame the first bag appears, i.e. BEFORE any click is physically possible; (b) the card re-derives its portrait EVERY FRAME — characterSheet.ts:341 `this.drawPortrait(v.portrait, x + PAD, top);` inside `draw`, which calls `const tex = this.portraitSource(spec);` at :602, with `this.portrait.visible = false` reset at :754 each frame. So any null window HEALS one frame after the fetch resolves, while the card is still open. The remaining window is (fetch latency − human reaction time) on the first bag of a page load, and it self-repairs on screen. That cannot present as the owner's persistent 'you don't have their image'.

verdicts.claim: evidence[1] — stinkTowerRenderer.ts:136 is the sibling contract, unconditional on the third line of `sync`; 'voltkinTowerRenderer.ts:470 and princessRenderer.ts:174 are identical in shape. stinkCloudRenderer is the only one of the four that defers its load behind a data condition — that asymmetry IS the finding.'
verdicts.note: The quote at stinkTowerRenderer.ts:133-136 is verbatim, and princessRenderer.ts:171-174 does match it. But voltkinTowerRenderer does NOT. I read src/render/voltkinTowerRenderer.ts:467-470 literally: `sync(world: World): void {` / `const chains = findAllVoltkinChains(world);` / `if (chains.length === 0 && this.sprites.size === 0) return;` / `this.ensureAtlas();`. That is exactly the data-dependent early return the report says is unique to stinkCloudRenderer — the researcher cited line 470 (`this.ensureAtlas();`) without reading line 469. Two more refute it further: towerRenderer.ts:254 calls `this.ensureAtlas(art);` INSIDE the per-spawner draw loop, below a fog `continue` at :252 — strictly more deferred than stinkCloud's; structureRampRenderer.ts:191 calls `this.ensureAtlas(spec.atlasBase);` inside `drawStructure`, i.e. only when that structure exists. Load-behind-data is the NORM in this renderer set (4 of 6), not an anomaly. The sentence 'that asymmetry IS the finding' is therefore false, and with it the report's framing of why this renderer is special.

verdicts.claim: fix_shape (1): move `this.ensureAtlas()` above the `stinkClouds.size === 0` early return. 'Cost: one 222 KB fetch per match that today happens a few seconds later anyway.'
verdicts.note: The cost statement is wrong in both directions. `sync` is called from the ticker at main.ts:4052 with NO gameState gate above it (the `PLAYING` block at :3951 closes at :3956), so the renderer syncs on the TITLE screen, from the first frame after page load. Moving `ensureAtlas()` above the early return therefore fetches 222,761 bytes at BOOT, for every visitor, on every page load — including the many matches where no stink tower is ever built, where today it is fetched NEVER. NO-ART — CONFIRMED, and I proved it harder than the report did rather than accepting its measurements.

WHAT I VERIFIED MYSELF, NOT FROM THE REPORT:
· `od -An -tu1 -j16 -N10 public/godly/stink-bag/anim/stink-bag-atlas.png` → `0 0 6 0 | 0 0 0 128 | 8 6`. That is IHDR width 0x00000600 = 1536, height 128, bit depth 8, colour type 6 = RGBA. The report's 1536x128 RGBA is exact.
· `cat public/godly/stink-bag/anim/stink-bag-anim.json` → cellW 128, cellH 128, footAnchor {x 0.5, y 0.9922}, `states.idle` {row 0, frames 12, ticksPerFrame 15}. 12 x 128 = 1536, so the manifest and the sheet agree to the pixel.
· `git ls-files --error-unmatch` on both files → exit 0. Both are present in `dist/` (222,761 bytes and 202 bytes). `public/**` is in deploy.yml's paths filter and the Pages job builds from a clean checkout, so they ship.
· INDEPENDENT SANITY CHECK THE REPORT DID NOT RUN: 222,761 bytes over 196,608 pixels is ~1.13 bytes/pixel after PNG compression. A blank cell, an alpha-only ghost wash or a flat placeholder compresses to a few hundred bytes. This is a dense, detailed image. I did not need a pixel toolchain to rule out an empty sheet.
· ⭐ AND THE RE-PACK FALLBACK IS REPRODUCIBLE FROM A CLEAN CLONE, WHICH THE REPORT ASSERTED WITHOUT CHECKING. `git ls-files assets-source/stink-bag/` lists all four clips as TRACKED — `clips/stink-bag/idle.mp4`, `clips/stink-bag-breathe/idle.mp4`, `clips/stink-bag-tight-a/idle.mp4` (740,098 bytes, the shipped one), `clips/stink-bag-tight-b/idle.mp4` — plus `atlas-spec.json`, `clip-spec.json`, `design-spec.json`, the owner reference `ref-bag-from-owner-tower.png`, four candidate stills a/b/c/d and the chosen `stink-bag-landed.png`, and the 281,540-byte `stink-bag-still.png`. `.gitignore` excludes only `assets-source/**/.req-*.json`, `.resp-*.json` and `*.raw`. So `node scripts/build-sprite-atlas.mjs assets-source/stink-bag/atlas-spec.json` works on any clone, at zero cost, forever.

WHAT I COULD NOT REPRODUCE, AND IT IS NOT LOAD-BEARING: the 38.3%-fully-opaque figure, the (8,10)-(116,127) bbox, the mean RGB (124,103,54) and the 2.6% ghost-wash band. Those need numpy/Pillow, which this run was not to install. Treat them as the researcher's claim, not as verified. Nothing in the fix depends on them.

No bag row. The bag's own sheet is the only art there is, and it is already the thing the accessor returns.

THREE REASONS IT WILL RUN BIGGER THAN 'well under 10K':
1. ⛔ THE LANE'S PREMISE IS UNSOUND, AND AN HONEST BRANCH WILL NOT STOP AT THE HARDENING. The fix as scoped almost certainly does not fix what the owner reported (see verdict 1 and the first three `missed` items). A branch that ships two lines and says 'done' is the S182 pattern. A branch that is honest will want to chase the real cause, and that is a different, larger job — and the only instrument that can see the card is a `@races`-lane Playwright observation the report itself declines. Scope the brief explicitly: SHIP THE FREE HALF, STATE PLAINLY THAT IT IS A HARDENING, ASK THE OWNER THE ONE DIAGNOSTIC QUESTION. That stays Micro. Anything else is Standard and needs its own PDR.
2. The test file lands nearer 120-180 lines than 90-120 once the world fixture, the seat/player setup `accentFor` needs, `resetConcealmentForTest()`, the IHDR `readUInt32BE` parse and the `\\r?\\n` CRLF handling are all in.

⛔ THE REPORT IS GOOD RESEARCH WITH A FALSE CENTRE. Its chain-walk is accurate hop by hop, its art finding is correct and is the most valuable thing in it, and it is admirably explicit that it never observed the live card. But the one claim the whole lane is built on — that stinkCloudRenderer is uniquely defective in deferring its atlas load — IS FALSE, and the mechanism it proposes cannot produce the symptom the owner described.

THE REFUTATION IN ONE LINE: voltkinTowerRenderer.ts:469 is `if (chains.length === 0 && this.sprites.size === 0) return;`, directly above the `this.ensureAtlas();` at :470 that the report quoted as proof of the opposite. towerRenderer.ts:254 and structureRampRenderer.ts:191 defer further still. The researcher read the line it wanted and not the line above it — which is, precisely, the failure mode this project's canon exists to prevent.

THE DEEPER PROBLEM IS TIMING, NOT SYMMETRY. Three facts I verified together close the case: `stinkCloudRenderer.sync` runs on every ticker frame from boot (main.ts:4052, outside the PLAYING gate at :3951-3956); a bag cannot be clicked until it is in `world.stinkClouds` (controls.ts:766); and the card re-queries `portraitSource` every single frame (characterSheet.ts:341 → :602, reset at :754). So the fetch starts on the frame the bag becomes clickable, the earliest possible click is a human reaction later, and any residual null repaints itself one frame after the fetch lands, while the card is still open. What the owner reported is persistent. What the report found is a sub-second flash that heals on screen.

AND HALF THE PROPOSED FIX IS A NET COST. Moving `ensureAtlas()` above the early return does not move a fetch a few seconds earlier — it moves it to the title screen, on every page load, for every visitor, in every match with no stink tower, where today it may never happen at all. That is a new unconditional 222 KB boot cost, against the grain of the S165/S169 lazy-atlas work the report cites as its own authority. ⭐ The other half — `this.ensureAtlas()` as the first line of `portraitTexture()` — is free, is strictly better, and closes the same window. Ship that alone.
